wods.title: Fast Lane
wods.hook: Week 2 starts in the fast lane. Short, sharp, done before your coffee cools. ☕🔥
wods.story: Two movements, three rounds, one rule: don't stop. Thrusters light up your legs and lungs at the same time, and the bike makes sure there's nowhere to hide. It's over quickly — that's exactly why it hurts.
wods.tip: Go unbroken on the 9s, no matter what. Break the 21s early (12 + 9) so you never stand over the dumbbells deciding.
wods.question: Sub-7 or survival mode? Drop your time 👀

wods.title: Pendulum
wods.scheme: Every minute on the minute, 4 rounds:
wods.scaled_short: DB 15/10 kg · ring rows · box step-ups · 12 sit-ups
wods.nogear_short: Jumping lunges · supermans · tuck jumps · sit-ups
wods.hook: Swing, pull, jump, breathe. Repeat until the clock says stop. ⏱️
wods.story: A steady back-and-forth Tuesday. Every minute asks one clear question — and gives you a little rest if you answer it fast. Great day to work on smooth, efficient reps instead of fast, messy ones.
wods.tip: Pull-ups: pick your strategy before the clock starts. If 10 unbroken isn't a sure thing, do 5 + 5 from round one — quick sets beat failed reps.
wods.question: Which minute was the toughest for you — snatch, pull, jump or sit-ups?

wods.title: Compromised
wods.scheme: As many rounds as possible in 20 min:
wods.scaled_short: 300 m runs · wall balls 4/3 kg · lighter lunges
wods.nogear_short: Air squats + walking lunges between the runs

plan.heading: RACE PLAN
plan.stimulus: Compromised running: every 400 m starts on tired legs. The goal is a run pace that barely changes from round 1 to the last round.
tips: Run at a pace you could talk at. You'll win this workout at the stations, not on the road.
Wall balls: unbroken if possible — one short break max, never two.
Lunges + broad jumps: steady rhythm, then head straight back out the door.

wods.hook: Midweek HYROX-style. Run, squat, lunge, jump — then run again on legs that don't want to. 🏃‍♀️
wods.story: This is what race day really feels like: not fast running, but running after everything else. Twenty minutes to learn how your legs behave when they're already cooked. Swipe for the scaling and the race plan →
wods.tip: Note your round count every lap. If one round takes 20 seconds longer than the first, you started too hot.
wods.question: How many rounds did you get — and which station broke your run pace?

wods.title: Pressure Point
wods.hook: Press. Burpee. Add three. Find out where your shoulders give up. 🪜
wods.story: The first rungs fly by and feel almost too easy. Then the bar gets heavier every time you pick it up, and the burpees stop being a rest. Somewhere around 12 reps the real workout starts.
wods.tip: Dip and drive with your legs — the push press is a leg movement that ends overhead. Shoulders alone won't get you to 15.
wods.question: Which rung did you finish on? Be honest 😅

wods.title: Tag Team
wods.scheme: For time · split reps any way · one works at a time:
wods.scaled_short: 1200 m relay · KB 16/12 kg · knee raises · lighter carry
wods.nogear_short: Relay run · jump squats · V-ups · synchro bear crawl

plan.heading: HOW IT WORKS
plan.stimulus: Run the relay first: one partner runs 400 m while the other rests, four legs total. Then split the swings and toes-to-bar however you like. The carry at the end? Both of you, side by side.
tips: Swings: switch every 10–15 reps. Short sets keep the bell moving.
Toes-to-bar: switch BEFORE your grip fails, not after.
Farmers carry: walk in step. If one of you drops the bells, you both stop.

wods.hook: Friday = tag team. Bring someone who won't let you walk the last lap. 🤝
wods.story: Split the work, share the suffering, high-five at the end. You rest while your partner works — and they're counting on you to be ready when they tag you. The farmers carry finishes it together, side by side.
wods.tip: Decide who runs first by who's the faster finisher. The stronger runner should take the 4th leg.
wods.question: Who's your tag team partner this week? Tag them 👇
wods.cta: Save it for Friday ⬇️ Post your team time in the comments.

wods.title: The Grind
wods.scheme: For time, one pass straight through:
wods.scaled_short: 750 m rows · KB 16/12 kg · incline push-ups · step-overs
wods.nogear_short: 1 km runs · air squats · burpee broad jumps · supermans

plan.heading: GAME PLAN
plan.stimulus: One long, steady effort. No round counting, no math — just chip away at each station until the list is empty.
tips: First row: 80% effort. You need that energy for the second one.
Squats and push-ups: sets of 10 with 5 breaths between. Never go to failure.
Second row is a race. Whatever you have left — spend it there.

wods.hook: Saturday. Six stations. One long grind. Bring snacks. 💜
wods.story: Chippers are honest workouts: you start at the top, you finish at the bottom, and there's no shortcut in between. Grab your crew, put on a good playlist and grind it out together. Swipe for the scaling and the game plan →
wods.tip: Break everything early and on purpose. The people who finish fastest are the ones who never sit down.
wods.question: How long did The Grind take you? Did the second row hurt more than the first?

wods.title: Reset Button
wods.scheme: 8 × (20 s work / 10 s rest) each · 1 min rest between:
wods.scaled_short: Skater steps · slow climbers · knee shoulder taps
wods.nogear_short: Already zero gear — living room, park, hotel room.
wods.target: Same reps in round 1 and round 8
wods.hook: Sunday reset. 16 minutes, one square metre of floor, zero excuses. 🌿
wods.story: After a big week, Sunday is about moving well, not moving to exhaustion. Hop side to side, climb, bridge and hold — your body will thank you on Monday.
wods.tip: Don't sprint the first 20 seconds. Pick a pace you can repeat eight times — that's the whole game.
wods.question: Where are you doing your Sunday reset today? 🏠🌳
